note: Uruguay distinguishes nationality, held only by birth, from 'legal citizenship', which carries the Uruguayan passport: under article 75 of the Constitution a foreigner of good conduct with capital, property, or a science, art or trade earns the right to legal citizenship after five years' habitual residence, three with a family established in Uruguay (modelled as five), its rights exercisable three years after the grant. GLOBALCIT (2024) codes no naturalisation for that reason and no loss of Uruguayan citizenship on taking another; nothing in article 75 asks for another citizenship to be given up.

sources.title: IMPO, Constitución de la República Oriental del Uruguay, artículo 75
sources.said: Tienen derecho a la ciudadanía legal: A) Los hombres y las mujeres extranjeros de buena conducta, con familia constituida en la República, que poseyendo algún capital en giro o propiedad en el país, o profesando alguna ciencia, arte o industria, tengan tres años de residencia habitual en la República. B) Los hombres y las mujeres extranjeros de buena conducta, sin familia constituida en la República, que tengan alguna de las cualidades del inciso anterior y cinco años de residencia habitual en el país.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Uruguay, 2024
sources.said: n.a. (Ex Const 75a-b, person can acquire 'legal citizenship' if he/she has had 3 years of habitual residence in Uruguay. Other conditions: good behaviour, have family in Uruguay (if not, 5 years' residence is required), and work participation or capital/property in Uruguay. Legal citizenship status cannot be equated with Urguayan citizenship.)
